messages.subject: DIANN-MSstats groupComparison Issue
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats team,

I have encountered an error when I am analysing DIANN protein-level DIA data in MSstats. I am able to carry out the conversion and data summarisation fine. But when I carry out the group comparison function, it finishes the calculations but then gives an error regarding 'undefined columns selected' (see below). The full data is quite large so I have cut it and this has given me the same error (see below). I have attached the files here.

model.no <http://model.no> <- groupComparison(contrast.matrix = comparison, data=quant.no <http://quant.no>, use_log_file = FALSE)
INFO  [2023-11-28 12:42:27]  == Start to test and get inference in whole plot ...
  |===============================================================================================================| 100%
INFO  [2023-11-28 12:42:28]  == Comparisons for all proteins are done.
Error in `[.data.frame`(as.data.frame(comparisons), , cols) :
  undefined columns selected

This indicates that there's probably something wrong with my 'comparison' matrix. So, I then tried to use MSstatsShiny, but this gave a similar message (see attached).

Has anyone seen this issue before?

On a separate note, I am finding that the Protein Level data groups are different from the Feature Level data groups (see below). Do you know what could cause this? This also happens with Proteome Discoverer data too. I have to manually change it in R.
> unique(quant.no <http://quant.no>$ProteinLevelData$GROUP)
[1] 10 ng  50 ng  200 ng 20 ng  5 ng
Levels: 5 ng 10 ng 20 ng 50 ng 200 ng
> unique(quant.no <http://quant.no>$FeatureLevelData$GROUP)
[1] 4 5 2 3 1
Levels: 1 2 3 4 5

I am using MSstats v4.10.0, MSConvert v1.12

Many thanks,
Amandeep

messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT missing value imputation bug: extreme logFC > 70
messages.subject_clean: MSstatsTMT missing value imputation bug: extreme logFC > 70
messages.body_plain:
Apologies for the delay in my response!

I've tested the following inputs
A.) keep only PSMs for protein in question
B.) randomly sample 2000 PSMs plus the PSMs for the protein in question
C.) the entirety of PSMs, meaning the original data frame
The protein in question is called "ABC123" (anonymized), I have seen similar issues in other experiments (these are 16 or 18plex TMT experiments of human cell lines with DMSO as control and small molecule treatments).

A and B resulted in reasonable log2FC, i.e. small changes around 0. Only C resulted in log2FC < 145 (see "output_running_r_script.txt"). Result C is reproducible.

Software version:
MSstatsTMT version 2.8.0
MSstats version 4.10.0
Also tried it with MSstatsTMT version 2.10.0, getting the same results.

I've attached the R script to reproduce the results, the input files for "A" and "B" (see above), as well as the output, highlighting the difference of dramatic log2FC (see below).
I hope this helps. Let me know should you need other info/data. I would be happy and grateful to know where the issue lies. Please keep me posted.

Many thanks for all your efforts !!

Best,
David

messages.subject: Re: DIANN-MSstats groupComparison Issue
messages.body_plain:
Hi Amandeep,

Sorry for the delay, this was a weird problem to solve. The problem is due to the lme4 package which we use to fit some statistical models in the groupComparison function. It has an issue with the older versions of the library Matrix that are not solved automatically on regular MSstats install. I was able to fix it by simply reinstalling lme4 from source:

install.packages("lme4", type = "source")

Let me know if this does not work. There is more information about this issue here:

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/77481539/error-in-initializeptr-function-cholmod-factor-ldeta-not-provided-by-pack

Best,
Devon

Notably, MSStat reports fold changes and p-values for some proteins that are missing more than 50% of data in each group. To illustrate this issue, here's an example. Please note that I encounter this issue (missing more than 50% of data in each group) across multiple groups, but not in the case of pairwise comparisons with only two conditions. However, differences in ratios between MSstat and manual calculations were observed in both scenarios.
I would appreciate your assistance in resolving this matter.
Best regards,
Thao

messages.body_plain:
Hello MSstats developers,

Firstly, thank you for providing us with Statistical tools and support.

My question regards the best normalization process to choose when dealing with different experiments and datasets. For example, is the experimental design important in the choice of normalization? If I have a basic comparison of two different groups with label free data do I have to apply a different normalization with respect to a time course experiment? Or it depends on the number of proteins involved?

Thank you very much again, I wish you a great day,
Giovanni

messages.subject_clean: MSstatsTMT missing value imputation bug: extreme logFC > 70
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mateusz / MSstats-users,

thank you so much for investigating the issue!!

In our pipeline I've implemented the following logic to circumvent the problem of exorbitant log-fold-changes due to imputation: for features of a protein check if any imputed value is higher/lower than the max/min of non-imputed features of that protein. If this is the case, then do not impute the values for any feature of that protein.

It would be great if a future release of MSstats(TMT) would have a solution for the issue. I'd expect this to lead to fewer missing values than my work-around.

Thank you for all your time and effort !!

Best,
David

messages.subject: Re: How to choose normalization?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Giovanni,

Your experimental design/assumptions in your data are very important when choosing the normalization method.

The main question when performing normalization is if you expect the majority of the proteins in your experiment to be changing across conditions or if you expect most to stay the same. If you expect most to stay the same (such as is generally the case in DIA) you are totally fine performing normalization via equalizing the medians (the default option in MSstats). If the experiment is more targeted (SRM/PRM) and you expect to see most of the proteins changing, you will most likely remove true biological variance from your experiment when performing normalization (bad).

The "gold standard" for normalization is to include some spike-in reference standards so that we can normalize to them. This obviously has to be done before you conduct the experiment however.

In terms of your second question, it most definitely has to do with the upstream data processing, not just normalization but how MSstats does missing value imputation, feature selection, and feature summarization. These upstream processing choices have a major impact on your final results.

TLDR; You are probably fine using the default normalization (equalize medians) since your experiment is DIA

Best,
Devon
